news.headline: Wells Fargo Raises uniQure Price Target to $75 as Wolfe Research Upgrades to Outperform
news.summary: Following uniQure's Q2 report, Wolfe Research upgraded the stock to Outperform (modeling a 70% probability of success for AMT-130 and $2 billion in peak U.S. sales), and Wells Fargo lifted its price target to $75, while Barclays trimmed its target to $60 but kept a Buy/Overweight rating.

news.headline: uniQure Announces Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Provides Company Update
news.summary: uniQure reported a Q2 net loss of $1.22/share (net loss ~$81.1 million) on revenue of $5.8 million, but shares rose after the company reaffirmed it had $810.3 million in cash as of June 30, 2026 (runway into 2030) and confirmed its AMT-130 BLA remains on track for submission in Q3 2026.

news.headline: uniQure Announces Closing of Upsized Public Offering and Full Exercise by Underwriters of Option to Purchase Additional Shares
news.summary: uniQure closed an upsized public offering of 5,686,813 ordinary shares at $45.50 each, including full exercise of the underwriters' option, raising roughly $259 million in gross proceeds to fund AMT-130 commercialization readiness and a confirmatory study.

news.headline: uniQure Announces Preliminary Data on the First Cohort in the Phase I/IIa Clinical Trial of AMT-260 in Refractory Mesial Temporal Lobe Epilepsy
news.summary: In six-month follow-up data from the first, low-dose cohort of AMT-260 presented at the Epilepsy Foundation Pipeline Conference, three of six patients saw disabling seizures drop 79%-100% from baseline, while the therapy was generally well tolerated with only mild-to-moderate adverse events.

news.headline: uniQure Announces Plan for BLA Submission for AMT-130 in Huntington's Disease
news.summary: After a Type B meeting, the FDA told uniQure that the ~3-year Phase I/II data can serve as the primary basis for an accelerated-approval BLA for AMT-130, reversing its earlier March 2026 stance; the company now plans to submit the BLA (with a requested priority review) in Q3 2026, pending alignment on a confirmatory study design.

catalysts.label: AMT-130 BLA submission to FDA
catalysts.detail: uniQure plans to submit its Biologics License Application for AMT-130 in Huntington's disease, seeking accelerated approval with priority review; a parallel U.K. MHRA submission is also planned for Q3 2026. Management reaffirmed this timeline on the July 29 Q2 earnings call.

catalysts.label: Four-year AMT-130 follow-up data readout
catalysts.detail: Topline four-year data from the low- and high-dose cohorts of the Phase I/II AMT-130 study are expected to be presented, updating on the 75% disease-progression slowing seen at 36 months.

catalysts.label: Potential FDA Advisory Committee (AdCom) meeting
catalysts.detail: Management has said an AdCom meeting is likely for the AMT-130 BLA, though the FDA has not formally requested one yet.

catalysts.label: AMT-260 second-cohort (higher-dose) epilepsy data
catalysts.detail: uniQure expects to report updated Phase I/IIa data including the higher-dose (3x10^12 gc/mL) second cohort of AMT-260 in refractory mesial temporal lobe epilepsy.

catalysts.label: Confirmatory study design agreement / initiation
catalysts.detail: uniQure must finalize with the FDA the design of a randomized, standard-of-care-controlled confirmatory study for AMT-130 as a post-approval commitment tied to accelerated approval.

pulse: uniQure shares (around $44, well off the 52-week high of $71.50 but far above the March 2026 low of $8.73) remain buoyed by the FDA's June 2026 reversal confirming that existing Phase I/II data can support an accelerated-approval BLA for AMT-130 in Huntington's disease, with submission still on track for Q3 2026 per the July 29 Q2 earnings update. The company holds $810.3 million in cash (runway into 2030) after a $259 million June follow-on offering, and Wall Street sentiment has kept improving into early August, with Wolfe Research upgrading to Outperform and Wells Fargo lifting its price target to $75 (Street consensus roughly $61-$71) despite continued heavy quarterly losses (~$81 million in Q2). The near-term trajectory now hinges on the actual BLA filing, September's four-year AMT-130 data update, and eventual clarity on an FDA advisory committee and confirmatory trial design.
